description: Our interests include cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, machine learning, software development and game development. We enjoy exploring challenging ideas and transforming them into practical solutions. We are a multidisciplinary team consisting of an Aerospace Engineer, Mechatronics Engineer, Digital Animation Artist, Software Engineer, and Cybersecurity specialist. I believe combining these different disciplines will allow us to approach challenges from multiple perspectives.
summary: We built N4S4 F0R FUN, an interactive, story-driven digital space museum for children aged about 8 to 12. It introduces them to the landers, rovers, descent stages and probes humanity has left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space, and to the science they made possible. Children explore a hand-drawn solar system, meet 22 machines through real NASA photos and short stories, and ask Astro, an AI tutor that answers only from checked NASA facts. In our Moon and Mars games, they catch, dig up and drive these machines, then learn what each one truly discovered. This answers the challenge by turning dense mission records into engaging stories that connect each machine’s engineering to the science it achieved. It matters because children usually only hear about today’s missions, while the explorers that paved the way are forgotten. We want them to feel connected to these machines and inspired to explore.
details:
Abandoned but not Forgotten is a story-driven digital space museum that helps children aged 8 to 12 discover 22 machines left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Children explore a hand-drawn solar system and open a page for each machine, showing a real NASA photo, its story and its sources. They can also slide through a mission timeline and ask Astro, an AI tutor that answers only from checked NASA facts. In two story games, they find Moon machines with a rocket claw and dig Mars machines out of bedrock, then plan rover drives that wait out the real signal delay to Mars. After each game they read what the machine truly discovered, take a quiz, and earn stars, badges and an unofficial certificate. The museum turns dense NASA records into hands-on stories, and every pretend part is clearly separated from the real history. Every fact comes from NASA and lists its sources, and the site has no ads, tracking or personal data. It works with a keyboard and screen readers, and it never implies NASA endorsement. We built it with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Python/FastAPI, the NASA Image and Video Library API, Supabase, Vercel, Render and GitHub. Claude Code helped write the code, and the demo narration is an AI-generated voice.
